items.message:
Now, I’ve let y’all nurse your hangovers off…. 💤 

So, here’s part III of V….

PUBLIC MONEY DOESN’T BECOME LESS PUBLIC BECAUSE THE DEAL HAS A PRETTY NAME. 💰

Now that you’ve seen most of the players, now we look at the paperwork…. 📋 

And, the CoastAL arrangement needs to be understood from a City of Orange Beach TAXPAYER’S side of the closing table. 

In 2021, the City announced a beachfront purchase alongside Orange Beach Land Company, owned by John McInnis and Cameron Price, the Flora-Bama co-owners. The announcement also identified the seller of the larger tract as 68 Ventures’ Nathan Cox.

Now, the announced cost for the City’s parcel and improvements was about $13 MILLION, roughly $10 million for the acquisition and another $3 million for improvements.

Public land and parking, but conveniently beside a PRIVATE restaurant development. 🏖️

The part that got missed by the TAXPAYERS and was conveniently glazed over by Tony Kennon was that the current recorded deed for this property references PREEXISTING 👏🏻 EASEMENTS 👏🏻 

Now, guess what those easements say they do……

To paraphrase, an easement existing and benefiting the City of Orange Beach for beach access and related work, including sand placement, vegetation, irrigation, and access structures to include bathrooms and outdoor showers.

We ALREADY had the SAME legal rights associated with that property.

To be clear, an easement and ownership give you different rights. 

So, the accounting starts with the access we already had, then identifies what additional ownership and control we purchased, what restrictions accompanied it, and what the private development received.

But, you don’t get to start the public’s side of the transaction at ZERO and sell us the whole thing as newly acquired access. 🧾

The City’s announced parking arrangement included approximately 107 resident-priority spaces during designated periods, another 56 spaces available for resident-exclusive use for limited days, and shared parking benefiting the adjacent development. 

The private company also had specified rights involving use and charging for some parking.

That’s more complicated than “we bought a beach parking lot.” 🫪

Who could use it? When? Who controlled it? Who could charge? What do  residents ACTUALLY receive when demand was highest?

What taxpayers gave up included MILLIONS of dollars available for other public needs. 🙈

What the arrangement committed included shared use of PUBLICLY supported property and improvements that helped a private business operate.

That’s a PRIVATE BUSINESS BENEFITING FROM PUBLIC INVESTMENT. 

You can call it support, an incentive, or a public-private arrangement, but you damn sure better account for it. 🚗

The City also obtained beach ownership and avoided the much larger condominium proposal. Those benefits belong in the calculation, too. 

But, so do the rights we already had, the parking restrictions, and the business benefits our spending helped provide.

“Historic investment” still needs an explanation of who got what.

Then came Beech’s and Pirate’s Voyage. 🏴‍☠️

Residents were being asked to consider traffic, drainage, trees, and a major attraction on the campground property. 

Then, after the worst case scenario was shoved down our throat and citizens revolted like the magical plan Tony Kennon had been orchestrating all along, the discussion shifted toward the City buying land…… 

Now, back to the players…. It’s been reported that John McInnis III held the underlying purchase contract at around $10 million, while the proposed City purchase was being discussed around $14 million.

Again, I’m no mathemagician, but that’s roughly a FOUR MILLION DOLLAR DIFFERENCE. ‼️

The contract and assignment terms matter to the final accounting. But, when TAXPAYERS are being considered as the buyer, the difference between the underlying price and the price offered to the City is something they’re entitled to understand.

Who actually held the contract when it was pitched to the city? Who stood to receive the spread? What did the council know? What was Tony negotiating, and with whom? Who else was there? 👀

By June 29th, the City and Pirate’s Voyage had withdrawn from the purchase negotiations. That proposed acquisition fell apart. The approximately $4 million was a proposed price difference, not a profit I’m saying somebody collected from the City.

The paperwork still matters. A transaction doesn’t become immune from scrutiny because public opposition helped make it untenable.

And the McInnis’s history with infrastructure reaches further back than CoastAL, doesn’t it? 📌

The McInnis family’s business interests included ownership in the original Foley Beach Express toll bridge venture, alongside the James family. 

John McInnis III has publicly discussed selling the bridge interests before his Flora-Bama involvement. Federal highway records document the original private bridge company, McInnis Corporation’s construction role, and the earlier sale to Macquarie. 📌

The James family was also the connection through which Cameron Price entered Flora-Bama ownership. 

That’s another relationship connecting the earlier business history to the people who later appeared together in the CoastAL and Orange Beach Land Company transactions. 📌

That’s a longstanding history involving PRIVATE COMMERCIAL INTERESTS and the infrastructure people use to reach this area. The bridge passed through later owners and eventually into state ownership. 🛣️

It belongs in the context because access, traffic, development, and commercial value are related. 

The SAME people involved in those transactions understood that relationship long before residents were being told what their roads could supposedly handle, didn’t they? 

So, when the same business interests appear around CoastAL, Beech’s, and discussions about public infrastructure, it’s NORMAL to want the underlying documents. But, ALDOT says they never existed. 

So, while no scrutiny was on, CoastAL closed. 

But, under slight pressure, both proposed Beech’s deals collapsed. And, y’all know the toll bridge and the new bridge has its own history. 🥴

But, “trust us” isn’t a substitute for any of them.

Part IV is what happened when ALL these relationships intersected with public office, school decisions, and the treatment of people asking questions. 🗺️ 

Jack Robertson, you’re up. 📱
